title: The Gospel, Divine Instruction, and the Mountain of God
english: By the guile of men in cunning. 6 Ps 1:5 The ungodly shall rise, but they shall not be judged, being self-condemned for being. For he who does not believe in me, he says, is already judged, having been shown to be condemned from his own unbelief. Ps 1:6a The deeds of the righteous are owned by God; for by this He knows them here. 7 Ps 1:6b Having been shown that the ungodly are not raised in judgment, it has been revealed how many of those sleeping in the dust of the earth are raised, some to eternal life, and others to eternal reproach and shame. For how is it that those being raised to be judged do not rise to eternal reproach and shame, the judgment itself making their sins manifest? If indeed this has become clear, why is it not said that all those sleeping in the dust of the earth are raised, some to eternal life, and others to eternal reproach and shame? For these things have been written concerning only those sinners coming unto judgment and the righteous being raised unto eternal life; of the ungodly, there is nothing of these being raised, nor will there be an examination of them after the resurrection. 8 Ps 2:8 Of all men moving by choice (for they are free agents), no one is essentially good or bad; and since the one possessing virtue is owned by God alone, and every such one becomes an inheritance of God. The whole of Israel was not good; it was said concerning him, 'He became a portion of the Lord, a branch of the inheritance of Israel Jacob.' It is shown that this nation did not only become an inheritance, but through goodness was so treated from what is said concerning God by the holy men: 'He chose for us His inheritance, the beauty of Jacob whom He loved.' If, however, one keeps the commandments and the faith toward God, one becomes an inheritance of God; the one transgressing the commandments of God and falling away from faith toward Him is cast out from such honor, just as he who turns from evil and does good becomes a lot of God even if he was not so before. This sequence remaining, he who formerly through godliness was an heir of God, Israel, becoming an apostate of God, fell away, not receiving the one who previously went before him in blessing, even as also for all other men, the Savior has come. It is necessary, therefore, that another, being fulfilled from many nations, should be brought in and approach...

It is said regarding the gospel: 'You will not add to me, and I will give you life instead of death' (cf. John 10:28), but it is not said of the Son; for it shows that he adds nothing to himself, but rather to those who are in need; just as to a physician and teacher things are given, so that they may become healthy and knowledgeable from him.

But also the saying 'The ends of the earth shall hold fast to you' is understood more simply: until the ends of the earth, his teaching shall prevail, the gospel being preached in all creation under the heaven. If it is possible for the ends of the earth to be called here, understand those who have passed through the earth in life and wisdom.

Ps 2:10: 'Now receive understanding, you risen from the dead who were crucified; and you, rulers, be instructed, knowing what you honored by surrounding with death, having risen, having loosed death' (Ps 2:9 allusion); for this will turn you to serve in fear, knowing what is being plotted against you, what God is, through which you have come. This slavery in fear will cease, having produced progress, so that divine exultation may come to you with trembling; for if any joy comes reasonably, it is exultation; but it does not happen before God with mere trembling. With this, 'Shout for joy to God with a voice of exultation, who is the Most High and awesome' (Ps 2:11 allusion) is consistent; for since the exultation is of the Most High and awesome, it is necessary to have it with trembling.

Ps 2:12a–c: The saying 'Seize instruction' is spoken in an extraordinary way, as if to be the follower of the phrase: 'Seize instruction quickly, and what you are encountering in this life, lest, while you are being sluggish, the Lord be angry and you perish from the way of righteousness' (Ps 2:12).

Ps 3:4: Since it was said that the psalm is proclaimed before the face of the Lord (Ps 3:4), it must be said that his head is also raised, the God who is, or that his divinity becomes manifest to the faithful through demonstration. The name of the head in these things signifies ruler; therefore, Christ, the ruler of men, is rightly their king of those being holy, and in this way he signifies their head.

Ps 3:5: His exceedingly high mountain is able to be a holy mountain of God, from which God hears those praying, his only-begotten Son, concerning whom it was said, 'The mountain of the Lord shall be visible at the end of days' (Ps 3:5), this word indicating the manifestation of what is to come according to...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Contemplative Aim and the Endurance of the Righteous
english: The epidemic at the end of the ages. Ps 3:6. To sleep signifies a reclining, after which sleep immediately follows. Since Jesus voluntarily laid down his soul, for this reason, having slept, he slumbered; for he would not have died if he had not given himself to this, and having been raised from the dead, being grasped by God, he has become the firstborn from the dead. Ps 3:8b. Vainly does one have enemies if he does not provide a pretext of hatred and enmity; such are all those persecuted for living piety in Christ Jesus, to whom it is said by the Savior, 'Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and lie every kind of evil against you on my account,' and the following. With this intention also David had many enemies in vain, such as Saul and Absalom and those with them; for having often shown much gentleness and goodness toward them for the holy one, they were enemies in vain. Ps 3:8c-9. Concerning such teeth, he often says to God, 'They have set their teeth against me,' and thanking that he was not harmed by them, he says, 'Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us into the prey of their teeth.' It is evident what he says concerning spiritual things. To those spoken of as 'biting,' who use [the teeth] badly, as the Galatians bite and devour one another, the teeth are called allegorically, being used vainly and sinfully with the powers of the soul. For when the petition is established, instead of enemies, friends and instead of sinners, diligent ones will be. The salvation of the Lord; therefore, let us not seek this from another, but from Him. And your good pleasure is upon your people; but what is the good pleasure coming upon the people, is it the will of the Father concerning the epidemic? Having shown the Savior who became man, he says, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' To this he will take [the power], and in your good pleasure our horn shall be exalted. Ps 4:1. An ode is a triumphal song, being uttered with a single voice, but a psalm is a hymn being struck with the instrument called the psalter or the lyre. If the ode, for the sake of leading upward, is an ode having become composed by thought alone, the psalm is a hymn with actions being performed according to the right reason, as if one having the practical life were singing, but the [spiritual]...
The text ends abruptly mid-clause.

The contemplative. Since now David perceives God and His truth with a pure heart, he utters a song, and he says that things are in the psalms because he has achieved much in a practical way. This song is that which they are accustomed to call the end, the most desired of his own things, while all other things are to be chosen and desired, but not for the sake of another; for it is the perfection of all things, concerning which also Paul says, 'If one has become like God, he will see Him' (1 John 3:2).

What, then, does the author intend by saying the song is for David but not written by David? Some say, then, that the psalm or the song belongs to David, but that he himself, having been inspired by God, brought it forward, while the song or the psalm belongs to David, but the things said have a reference to him. And often what is announced belongs both to him and to him; either that which is being suggested was foretold by him through his ministry of the Spirit, or that the psalm being given to someone who sings was announced to David through them. Whichever it may be of those written in the Scriptures, it is known only to the one who is wise according to God.

But God is enlarged in affliction, not ceasing the pressure, not overthrowing the evildoers, but providing magnanimity to bear the circumstances bravely (Ps 4:2b). This is the mindset that should be heard. And many afflictions of the righteous, and from all of them He will rescue them, granting endurance (Ps 4:3). And he who also, even outside of circumstances, makes himself a magnanimous man, standing against the circumstances like Joseph and Job, but also himself standing against what lies ahead.

And many such things are borne also in the Scripture, for it is said, 'The mortal is born of a woman' (Ps 4:4a), and in [John] 'Among those born of women, none is greater than John' (John 1:23). For these words are spoken instead of 'man.' The saint of God is not to be wondered at if he bears afflictions magnanimously, which seem to be beyond man, but also if he, calling upon God, should immediately have a rebuke, whereas the heavy-hearted man ignores everything, that is, having a mindset with malice; if the word was spoken concerning Christ to the Jews, because the heavy-hearted are not children of God but of men, how...

title: Inheritance and the Vision of Light
english: For the Lord did not marvel at the Holy One in him and through him, having fulfilled the prophecies, with extraordinary powers occurring through him, and also having risen from the dead. But you will know, having cast off the heavy heart and having searched the writings concerning the Holy One; for the newness of the Spirit will be found searching for you.

Having received this word, the apostle brought it to it: 'Let not the sun go down on your anger, nor give place to the devil' (Ephesians 4:26). He who has received this apostolic exhortation, being angry, does not sin by persisting in staying angry and calling it monthly anger. This thought is confirmed by what follows: 'For you say' (clearly being angry) 'in your hearts, strike upon your beds, so as to have risen from sleep and to have done or said nothing of those in the heart covered in anger' (Psalm 4:4).

It is possible to call the Light of the face of God the character of the substance and the icon of the invisible God, through which light it was signaled toward us, having been formed according to Him (Psalm 4:6). It should not be ignored how some read 'Who will show us the good things thus'; the good things are not of many, but it is of one to show; and he is the only-begotten Son of God. By 'thus' they take 'Who' as signifying specifically what is unique and one in number in essence. It is conjoined with the witness 'A certain noble man', for there the 'Who' signifies what is uniquely such.

Even if you do not receive glory from the pleasures of yourselves, but I, expecting an age to come and the reward of upright citizenship, having become free from all disturbance through hope, 'I will sleep and lie down also' (Psalm 4:8), saying the departure from life; giving the reason for having slept and having slumbered in peace, he immediately brought to it 'You have settled me on hope' (Psalm 4:9). It is also said in the Psalms toward the soul from the face of God, 'I will dwell in hope'. God does this, proposing the hope of coming divine good things to those dwelling by Him in intellectual and practical virtue and in doctrines of truth and ecclesiastical laws.
Toward the end, gracious to you...

He prays for the soul being brought forward, that the church might be prepared for a divine inheritance for those who are healers of God; for inheritance belongs to those being healed by the Lord. But this inheritance is not corruptible and does not possess being in sensible wealth; for it is said that the heirs of this are to be brought into an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading, kept in the heavens (1 Peter 1:4). Into this, the Savior calls the worthy: 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you' (Matthew 25:34). Having received this, the one speaking the present psalm says he is sending a prayer to the one who has made it favorable to God, that he might be worthy to be shown an heir of it according to the New Covenant, just as he signifies concerning his own soul by the inscription 'For the one inheriting.'

As for 'To enlighten,' it is not used in a common way; in the Scripture, it constantly signifies receiving into the ears the words being announced by the speaker because of their nearness. It is said that the righteous are near to God, that God hearkens to the prayers of the righteous and has them in his heed for their supplication (Psalm 5:2-3). And God turns out to be a King and Creator of those who have not stretched out their hands toward a foreign god, nor are they ruled by sin.

According to theory, then: to whom the sun of righteousness has risen, having come into being at the beginning of an intelligible day, bringing a gift of grace to the cause of illumination. 'In the morning,' he says, 'hearkening to my voice' (Psalm 30:4); for to whom must one confess such a great good, O Lord, regarding the one who caused light to rise for me, existing as the greatest vision? For he always enters into the visions that are to be and desires to see the beauties of the truth. This is also presented from the 'And I shall see.' For just as 'I am coming' signifies unceasing approach, so 'I shall see' manifests an ever-increasing comprehension; for how can he who has obtained the promise not always see, 'The Lord shall be your eternal light, and Light to the righteous always' (Isaiah 60:19; Malachi 4:2)? And there is another scripture possessing 'I shall present to you and you shall see me,' which does not speak of all, but of those speaking with boldness according to the great Elijah because of their departure from the polity.
